tips.t01:
Before dialysis, CKD stages 3–5 usually call for less protein.
Your own target comes from your profile.
tips.t02:
Keep salt under 5 g a day.
Leaving the broth behind makes a real difference.
tips.t03:
Vegetables can be high in potassium too.
Blanching them first helps.
tips.t04: Phosphorus in processed foods is absorbed more easily, so it needs extra care.
tips.t05:
Cutting protein out entirely can lead to malnutrition.
The right amount matters.
tips.t06: Logging meals for just three days shows your average sodium intake.
tips.t07: Your eating pattern over the past month can be linked to changes in GFR.
tips.t08: Keeping a steady record can help slow the decline of kidney function.
tips.t09: Managing meals together with family raises the odds of sticking with it.
tips.t10: Potassium can swing within a single day depending on what you eat.
tips.t11: High phosphorus levels can be linked to itching.
tips.t12: Too much sodium affects blood pressure and can lower GFR.
tips.t13: A sudden jump in weight can be a sign of fluid retention.
tips.t14: We estimate potassium, phosphorus, and sodium from the ingredients in your photo.
tips.t15: The same foods combined differently can change the nutrition risk.
tips.t16: Even the same dish can burden the kidneys differently depending on how it's cooked.
